## Use Pythagoras
The longest side, $5x - 9$, is the hypotenuse (opposite the right angle).
(5x-9)^2 &= (x-1)^2 + (4x)^2
## Expand both sides
25x^2 - 90x + 81 &= x^2 - 2x + 1 + 16x^2
25x^2 - 90x + 81 &= 17x^2 - 2x + 1
## Collect all terms on one side
8x^2 - 88x + 80 &= 0
## Divide by 8
x^2 - 11x + 10 &= 0
## Factorise
(x-1)(x-10) &= 0
x = 1 \text{ or } x &= 10
## Reject x = 1
If $x = 1$, the side $x - 1$ would be 0, which is impossible.
x &= 10
ANSWER: x = 10

## Find the three sides when x = 10
x - 1 &= 10 - 1 = 9
4x &= 4(10) = 40
5x - 9 &= 5(10) - 9 = 41
## Check Pythagoras for 9, 40, 41
9^2 + 40^2 &= 81 + 1600
&= 1681
41^2 &= 1681
Since $9^2 + 40^2 = 41^2$, the sides 9, 40, 41 form a pythagorean triple.
ANSWER: 9^2 + 40^2 = 41^2

## Assume two inputs give the same output
$f$ is injective if $f(a) = f(b)$ forces $a = b$.
f(a) &= f(b)
3a - 2 &= 3b - 2
## Solve for a
3a &= 3b
a &= b
Different inputs always give different outputs, so $f$ is injective.
ANSWER: f(a) = f(b) \Rightarrow a = b \text{, so } f \text{ is injective}

## Set up the product rule
$y = uv$ with $u = x$ and $v = \sin\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$, so $\frac{dy}{dx} = u\frac{dv}{dx} + v\frac{du}{dx}$.
\frac{du}{dx} &= 1
## Differentiate v with the chain rule
Write $\frac{1}{x} = x^{-1}$, which differentiates to $-\frac{1}{x^2}$.
\frac{dv}{dx} &= \cos\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)
## Combine
\frac{dy}{dx} &= x\cos\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{x^2}\right) + \sin\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)(1)
&= \sin\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) - \frac{1}{x}\cos\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)
## Substitute x = 4/pi
When $x = \frac{4}{\pi}$, $\frac{1}{x} = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
\frac{dy}{dx} &= \sin\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{4}\cos\frac{\pi}{4}
## Evaluate in radians
Put the calculator in radian mode.
\frac{dy}{dx} &= 0.7071 - 0.5554
&\approx 0.15
ANSWER: 0.15

## Set f(x) = 0 (the ball is on the ground)
-x^2 + 10x &= 0
## Factorise and solve
x(-x + 10) &= 0
x = 0 \quad &\text{or} \quad -x + 10 = 0
x &= 0 \text{ or } x = 10
ANSWER: x = 0 \text{ m} \text{ or } x = 10 \text{ m}

## Find the slope of the path at B
The slope at $x = 4.5$ is $f'(4.5)$, and slope $= \tan\theta$.
\tan\theta &= f'(4.5)
&= -0.548(4.5) + 1.193
&= -2.466 + 1.193
&= -1.273
## Find the acute angle
The slope is negative because the ball is coming down, so take the positive value for the acute angle.
\theta &= \tan^{-1}(1.273)
&= 51.8^\circ
&\approx 52^\circ
ANSWER: 52^\circ

## Find the translation that maps A onto C
A(-0.5,\ 2.565) &\to C(0,\ 2)
x\text{-shift} &= 0 - (-0.5) = 0.5
y\text{-shift} &= 2 - 2.565 = -0.565
## Apply the translation to the maximum point (2.177, 4.529)
Use the maximum height from part (i); the translation moves every point of the curve the same way.
x &= 2.177 + 0.5
&= 2.677
y &= 4.529 - 0.565
&= 3.964
ANSWER: (2.677,\ 3.964)

## Apply the rules to G4 to get G5
A female has two children in the next generation: a female (upper) and a male (lower). A male has just one: a female, straight across.
## Continue each entry in G4
The upper Female in G4 gives a Female above and a Male below.
The Male in G4 gives one Female straight across.
The lower Female in G4 gives a Female and a Male as well.
## Read off G5
From top to bottom, G5 is: Female, Male, Female, Female, Male (5 bees).
ANSWER: G_5 = \text{Female, Male, Female, Female, Male}

## Read G4 and G5 from the diagram
$G_4 = 3$ (three bees) and $G_5 = 5$ (five bees).
## Find G6
G_6 &= G_5 + G_4
&= 5 + 3
&= 8
## Find G7
G_7 &= G_6 + G_5
&= 8 + 5
&= 13
ANSWER: G_6 = 8,\ G_7 = 13

## Expand (1 + √5)³
(1+\sqrt5)^3 &= 1 + 3\sqrt5 + 3(\sqrt5)^2 + (\sqrt5)^3
&= 1 + 3\sqrt5 + 15 + 5\sqrt5
&= 16 + 8\sqrt5
## Expand (1 − √5)³
(1-\sqrt5)^3 &= 1 - 3\sqrt5 + 3(\sqrt5)^2 - (\sqrt5)^3
&= 1 - 3\sqrt5 + 15 - 5\sqrt5
&= 16 - 8\sqrt5
## Subtract to get the numerator
(1+\sqrt5)^3 - (1-\sqrt5)^3 &= (16 + 8\sqrt5) - (16 - 8\sqrt5)
&= 16\sqrt5
## Substitute n = 3 and simplify
G_3 &= \frac{16\sqrt5}{2^3\sqrt5}
&= \frac{16\sqrt5}{8\sqrt5}
&= 2
ANSWER: G_3 = 2

## Find the slope of AC
Use $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ with $A(6, -2)$ and $C(-3, 4)$.
\text{Slope } AC &= \frac{4 - (-2)}{-3 - 6}
&= \frac{6}{-9}
&= -\frac{2}{3}
## Find the perpendicular slope
Perpendicular slopes multiply to $-1$, so turn the slope upside down and change its sign.
\text{Perpendicular slope} &= \frac{3}{2}
## Write the line through B(5, 3)
y - 3 &= \frac{3}{2}(x - 5)
2(y - 3) &= 3(x - 5)
2y - 6 &= 3x - 15
3x - 2y &= 9
ANSWER: 3x - 2y = 9

## Plan: intersect two altitudes
The orthocentre is where the altitudes meet. The altitude from $B$ is the line from part (a): $3x - 2y = 9$.
Find a second altitude, from $C$ perpendicular to $AB$.
## Find the slope of AB
\text{Slope } AB &= \frac{3 - (-2)}{5 - 6}
&= \frac{5}{-1}
&= -5
## Find the perpendicular slope
\text{Perpendicular slope} &= \frac{1}{5}
## Write the altitude from C(-3, 4)
y - 4 &= \frac{1}{5}(x + 3)
5(y - 4) &= x + 3
5y - 20 &= x + 3
x - 5y &= -23
## Solve the two altitudes together
3x - 2y &= 9
x &= 5y - 23
Substitute $x = 5y - 23$ into $3x - 2y = 9$.
3(5y - 23) - 2y &= 9
15y - 69 - 2y &= 9
13y &= 78
y &= 6
x &= 5(6) - 23
x &= 7
ANSWER: (7, 6)

## Use the point-slope formula with X(-1, 6)
y - 6 &= \frac{1}{7}(x + 1)
7(y - 6) &= x + 1
7y - 42 &= x + 1
## Move everything to one side
0 &= x - 7y + 1 + 42
x - 7y + 43 &= 0
ANSWER: x - 7y + 43 = 0

## Set up the distance from C to the tangent
The centre is $C(-g, -f)$. The radius $5$ equals the perpendicular distance from $C$ to $l: 3x + 4y - 21 = 0$.
Use $D = \frac{|ax_1 + by_1 + c|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$ with $x_1 = -g$, $y_1 = -f$.
5 &= \frac{|3(-g) + 4(-f) - 21|}{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}}
5 &= \frac{|-3g - 4f - 21|}{5}
25 &= |-3g - 4f - 21|
## Remove the modulus (two cases)
-3g - 4f - 21 &= 25 \quad \text{or} \quad -3g - 4f - 21 = -25
3g + 4f &= -46 \quad \text{or} \quad 3g + 4f = 4
## Use the fact that C lies on XC
$C(-g, -f)$ is on the line $x - 7y + 43 = 0$ from part (a).
-g + 7f + 43 &= 0
g &= 7f + 43
## Solve for one circle using 3g + 4f = -46
Take $3g + 4f = -46$ and substitute $g = 7f + 43$.
3(7f + 43) + 4f &= -46
21f + 129 + 4f &= -46
25f &= -175
f &= -7
g &= 7(-7) + 43
g &= -6
## Write the equation of the circle
The centre is $(-g, -f) = (6, 7)$ and the radius is $5$.
(x - 6)^2 + (y - 7)^2 &= 5^2
(x - 6)^2 + (y - 7)^2 &= 25
The other case, $3g + 4f = 4$, gives $g = 8$, $f = -5$ and the circle $(x+8)^2 + (y-5)^2 = 25$.
ANSWER: (x - 6)^2 + (y - 7)^2 = 25

## Find a right angle in each triangle
$[BD] \perp [AC]$, so both triangles have a right angle at $B$.
|\angle ABD| &= |\angle CBD| = 90^\circ
## Use the angle in a semicircle
The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so $\angle ADC$ is $90^\circ$.
|\angle ADB| + |\angle BDC| &= 90^\circ
## Use the angle sum in triangle DBC
Angles in triangle $DBC$ add to $180^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = 90^\circ$.
|\angle BDC| + |\angle BCD| &= 90^\circ
## Compare the two equations
Both sums equal $90^\circ$ and both contain $|\angle BDC|$.
|\angle ADB| + |\angle BDC| &= |\angle BDC| + |\angle BCD|
Subtract $|\angle BDC|$ from both sides.
|\angle ADB| &= |\angle BCD|
## State the conclusion
Two angles of $ABD$ equal two angles of $DBC$ ($90^\circ$ at $B$, and $\angle ADB = \angle BCD$), so the triangles are equiangular, hence similar.
ANSWER: \triangle ABD \text{ and } \triangle DBC \text{ are similar}

## Set up the lengths from part (a)(ii)
In part (a)(ii) $|AB| = x$, $|BC| = 1$ gives $|BD| = \sqrt{x}$. Let $x = |TU|$ in cm.
## Extend [TU] by 1 cm
Extend $[TU]$ beyond $U$ to a point $P$ with $|UP| = 1$ cm. Then $|TP| = |TU| + 1$.
## Draw the semicircle on [TP]
Construct the midpoint of $[TP]$ with the perpendicular bisector (arcs from $T$ and $P$). Draw the circle with $[TP]$ as diameter.
## Draw the perpendicular at U
Construct the perpendicular to $[TP]$ at $U$ and mark where it meets the circle. This length is $\sqrt{|TU|}$ cm, since $T, U, P$ play the roles of $A, B, C$.
ANSWER: \text{Perpendicular at } U \text{ to the circle has length } \sqrt{|TU|} \text{ cm}

## List the ways exactly two of them hit
Way 1 is given: John and David hit, Mike misses. Swap which one misses to get the other two-hit ways.
## Add the way all three hit
Winning needs at least two hits, so all three hitting is the fourth way. This gives four ways in total.
ANSWER: \text{Ways: (\checkmark \checkmark \times ), (\checkmark \times \checkmark ), (\times \checkmark \checkmark ), (\checkmark \checkmark \checkmark )}

## Write P(A) and P(B) from the diagram
P(A) &= x + 0.1
P(B) &= 0.1 + 0.3 = 0.4
## Use the rule for independent events
$A$ and $B$ are independent when $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$.
0.1 &= (x + 0.1) \times 0.4
## Solve for x
0.1 &= 0.4x + 0.04
0.06 &= 0.4x
x &= \frac{0.06}{0.4}
x &= 0.15
ANSWER: P(A) = x + 0.1,\quad x = 0.15
